📝 Notes

R&D daily sprint

Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Gabor Kerekes is investigating the technical feasibility of wrapping the application for iOS, particularly focusing on Apple's App Store approval for non-native elements, which Amir Houieh described as potentially clunky, while both agreed testing the process would be quick. Gabor Kerekes has finalized the prototype documentation for Amir Houieh's use and committed to pushing the repository so Amir Houieh and Noémi Biró can review it, while Amir Houieh noted their focus on refactoring "the brain thing," agreeing that using the brain will help define the prototype's use case. The participants decided to plan a meeting on Monday to establish the timeline and goals for the Sibil project and discuss Mycelium updates, while also brainstorming alternative names for the "brain" component, such as Mycorisa, but ultimately decided to continue the search for a better name.
Details
iOS App Wrapping Feasibility: Gabor Kerekes is researching the technical feasibility of wrapping the application for iOS, noting that the difficulty lies less in the technical execution and more in gaining approval from Apple, specifically if they allow such apps in the App Store without native elements. Amir Houieh mentioned that running it on Chrome V8 or a wrapper "feels a bit clunky," and Gabor Kerekes clarified it would be similar to installing a progressive web app but from the App Store. They agreed that testing the process should only take a day or two (00:00:00).
Prototype Status and Workshop Decision: Gabor Kerekes has cleaned up the prototype's documentation and plans to push the repository so Amir Houieh can utilize it. The discussion shifted to whether to hold a joint workshop on the prototype today, with Gabor Kerekes indicating they have ideas but is open to prototyping together for new insights, and Amir Houieh mentioning they were focused on a major refactor of "the brain thing" (00:02:04). Both Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh are fine with either working together or individually on the prototype (00:05:54).
Approach to Prototype Development and Brain Integration: Amir Houieh indicated that to properly integrate the brain, they prefer to have the prototype's repository to build a use case and present how it works. Gabor Kerekes mentioned that the prototype is currently only a mockup and that the entire use case is still evolving and in flux (00:03:34). They agreed that attempting to use the brain for the project will likely help define the use case rather than the other way around (00:04:42).
Next Steps for Prototype Work: Noémi Biró suggested that Gabor Kerekes should first develop some further ideas before engaging the team, which Gabor Kerekes agreed to do, noting they will "flush them out". Gabor Kerekes committed to pushing the repository so Amir Houieh and Noémi Biró can run it and provide feedback, potentially leading to a call if issues arise (00:05:54). Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh concluded the meeting by committing to work on the prototype and the "brain/nexus/razor" respectively (00:08:15).
Planning for Monday's Meeting and Mycelium Project: The team decided to plan a meeting on Monday following the daily to establish a timeline, specific goals, and outcomes for the Sibil project. They plan to extend the daily meeting, spending about an hour on the Sibil overview and then further discussing Mycelium, which will include updates from Amir Houieh (00:07:02). Noémi Biró noted they need about an hour to finish work on the website before Amir Houieh can publish it (00:08:15).
Brainstorming Project Naming: The team engaged in brainstorming for a better name for the "brain" component, which is currently referred to as Nexus or Razor. Amir Houieh suggested the name should be inspired by Mycelium, and Noémi Biró proposed "Mycorisa," though Gabor Kerekes found it difficult to pronounce and not catchy. The team agreed to keep brainstorming for a better name, with Gabor Kerekes noting they might explore specific mushroom species for inspiration (00:08:15).
Suggested next steps
Gabor Kerekes will flush out ideas for the prototype and push the repo so Amir Houieh can use it.
Noémi Biró will work on the website for one more hour before Amir Houieh publishes it.
Amir Houieh will finish the major refactor on top of the brain.
The group will extend the daily meeting on Monday to plan a timeline for Sibil and define specific goals and outcomes.
